messages:
pagerbot: :rotating_light: SECURITY ALERT: unusual auth token reuse detected across multiple edge proxies. Suspicious replay pattern (401 -> 200) from 3 IPs. Rule: auth.replay.pattern5.

alex (on-call): acknowledge. digging in. @lee can you pull recent edge auth logs for window 2025-11-02T01:00Z-01:10Z?

lee (sre): pulling now. grepping S3 logs. saw repeated requests with same Authorization header. sample:
```
edge-logs/2025-11-02/01:02:11 proxy1 GET /v1/generate 200 Authorization: Bearer sk-live-***-abcd1234
edge-logs/2025-11-02/01:02:12 proxy2 GET /v1/generate 200 Authorization: Bearer sk-live-***-abcd1234
```
Looks like a long-lived service key used from different regions.

sam (security): :lock: escalate. That `sk-live-*` pattern maps to long-lived service keys. @maria can you check recent deployment/key changes? any tickets mentioning `svc-ingest` or manual key uploads?

maria (support): nothing in support tickets. There was a staging token rotation yesterday but not matching this pattern. Reaching out to infra deploy owners now.

alex (on-call): immediate mitigations: 1) block the three source IPs at edge WAF 2) add temporary rate-limit for requests with Authorization `sk-live-*` 3) prepare rotation for impacted service token(s) and revoke sessions. @lee start the edge blocks, @sam prepare rotation steps.

lee (sre): blocked IPs 18.203.45.12, 3.120.98.4, 52.14.22.9 at edge WAF. Added header-based rate limit (10r/s) for Authorization pattern. Watching metric streams for error spikes. :white_check_mark: 

sam (security): preparing rotation. Which principals? logs indicate `svc-ingest` used for artifact fetches. Recommend: create replacement key, update canary/staging then prod, then revoke old key after rollout. Also start forensics on hosts that used the key.

ingrid (product): any customer-facing failures or elevated 4xx/5xx? Could be data-read impact if tokens were reused.

lee (sre): some GETs to /artifacts/public/ succeeded. No obvious hits to PII endpoints in initial scan. Still correlating object access logs to user accounts.

sam (security): legal heads-up: @kate, possible leak of Authorization headers via logs or exfil. If keys were exfiltrated we may need to notify customers. Recommend hold on customer comms until scope clearer.

kate (legal): received. preserve all artifacts. do not send external notifications yet. prepare timeline and classification (accidental exposure vs exfiltration).

alex (on-call): action items: @lee full scan for other `sk-live-` instances (`grep -R \"sk-live-\" edge-logs/ | wc -l`), @sam run IAM rotation playbook, @maria draft customer-impact template, @kate standby. I'll update exec and open bridge if scope widens.

lee (sre): running scan. preliminary counts: 13 unique token instances across 7 hosts between 01:00-01:10Z. Collating host list now.

sam (security): telemetry shows outbound connection from host `ingest-prod-3` to external IP 3.120.98.4 during spike window. Starting live forensics pull (disk + network).

maria (support): drafting customer note template: short, factual, remediation steps taken, next steps. Will wait for final scope before sending.

alex (on-call): handoff at 02:00Z to @sam (overnight). If any confirmed data exposure escalate to Sev1 and notify CSMs + legal. Currently holding at Sev2.

pagerbot: incident created: incident/2025-11-02-auth-replay-1759012345. PagerDuty: sam_tier1 notified.

sam (security): acknowledged takeover. continuing collection and will post update in 15m.

lee (sre): scan complete. sanitized token host list pushed to artifacts bucket: `s3://incidents/1759012345/keys.txt` (contains host IDs: ingest-prod-1, ingest-prod-3, proxy2, proxy5, proxy7, etc.).

alex (on-call): thanks all. keep thread to short status updates only. :eyes:
